stem:
Esha finds $15\%$ of $80$ mentally using benchmark percentages.

Which method is correct?

options.text: Call "same whole" the finished answer, without computing any percent of $80$.
Add $10\%$ of $80$ to $5\%$ of a different value, skipping that the benchmarks must share the same whole.
Use the same benchmark story to compare lengths on an unrelated map scale.

teacher.key_rationale: Benchmark percents of the same value combine: $10\%+5\%=15\%$ of $80$ gives $8+4=12$. Relabelling without computing, mixing different wholes, or switching to map scales all miss that shared-whole decomposition.
